description: Caliper Docker 5-orderer Raft sweep at rates 100/500/1000/2000 tx/s with 5 seeds × 4 rounds × 60s each.
network: 5-orderer Raft (orderer1-5), 2 peers (org1, org2), channel mychannel, chaincode basic v1.0 with endorsement policy OR(Org1MSP.peer, Org2MSP.peer)
workload: CreateAsset(unique_id, color=red, size=100, owner=alice, value=42) via Fabric Gateway SDK
outcome: PARTIAL SUCCESS - critical findings on saturation point

rate-1000.note: saturation point identified - >50% commits time out

rate-2000.note: complete saturation, but Caliper still detects max network throughput ~453

seeds_2_3_4.diagnosis: Network entered degraded state after seed 1's rate-2000 saturation. Orderer Raft cluster reports forwarding timeouts to follower nodes (see orderer1 logs at 14:10 UTC showing 'rejected by Order: timed out (7s) waiting on forwarding to 3'). Peers accumulated ~68k assets in seed 1, slowing state DB operations beyond Caliper's commit timeout window. Seed 5 was stopped mid-round 2 with same DEADLINE_EXCEEDED pattern.

key_findings.validated_throughput: 5-orderer Raft + 2 peers + basic chaincode sustains 500 TPS with 530 ms avg latency on commodity Docker Desktop
key_findings.saturation_point: ~500-700 TPS — above this, commit latency explodes from 530 ms to 33 s
key_findings.raft_overhead_visible: Orderer leader-to-follower forwarding becomes bottleneck under load; matches Raft theoretical commit cost
key_findings.0_safety_violations: All successful transactions in seed 1 produced valid ledger entries (block 88468+ reached)

data_caveats: Only seed 1 yields paper-grade clean numbers; seeds 2-4 are diagnostic data showing system overload
txDuration=60s/round was too long; would need 30s/round + cool-down between seeds for clean 5-seed replication
Local Docker Desktop is the bottleneck (CPU+memory shared with WSL2 + Caliper container)
Real production AWS deployment would shift saturation higher
All recorded ledger height milestones preserved in caliper-seed*.log files

files.report-seed1.html: Caliper-generated HTML report (15 KB), seed 1, all 4 rates
files.caliper-seed1.log: Full Caliper debug log, seed 1 (~35 MB)

paper_integration.paper_table_label: honest disclosure paragraph in §VII.B (seeds 2-5 cumulative state-DB bottleneck)

related_phases.delta: 5node_saturation_delta_2026-06-08 (reinterprets beta's rate-1000 45% timeouts as Caliper 7s window expiration, NOT actual blockchain failure)

paper_integration.delta_reinterpretation: Beta's rate-1000 45% commit timeouts are now understood as the Caliper SDK's default 7-second observation window being exceeded once tail latency grows past it. Delta sweep at rates 600-900 tx/s shows 0 commit failures across 270,013 transactions, demonstrating the blockchain DOES commit them — just outside the SDK's observation window. The 'saturation point at ~500-700 TPS' in v49 is therefore narrowed by delta to ~530 TPS plateau.
